title: A journey into change
paragraphs: When Korean officials traveled to Japan during the period of opening, they encountered a neighboring country undergoing extensive institutional and technological change. Such visits were not tourism in the modern sense. They were diplomatic missions and opportunities to observe arrangements that might bear upon the pressures confronting Joseon itself. The travelers had to translate unfamiliar sights into reports their colleagues could use.

The question was never simply whether Japan had become modern. Delegates examined specific practices, from administrative organization to the visible transformation of towns and transport. What they saw was filtered through the limited time of a mission, the people they met, and the political arguments already unfolding at home.
